newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil trades a little lower.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil trades a little lower.

text.p: European low-sulphur straight run traded slightly lower at the end of the week, with sellers said to be cutting their prices with cargoes getting prompter.
A Scandinavian refiner said he sold a July 5-10 cargo of 25,000 to 30,000 tonnes to a U.S. buyer at a price between $97/$99 fob. This compared with a cargo traded last week at $99 fob.
The cargo is co-loading with another cargo in the north on a fob basis, the seller said.
"The numbers are a bit lower as the cargoes are getting prompter and prompter," the refiner said, commenting on sellers cutting their prices a little from three figures earlier this week.
He said he even heard a bid at $102 cif from a French refiner.
However, a second seller said that he turned down bids of $97 adding he would still like to see about $100 or more as there are not that many buyers on the market.
Traders were mixed over Russian high-sulphur straight run with some saying they were shown at higher prices while others said it was steady.

Two pieces, an M-100 and M-100/E4, were being actively shown. Some traders said the former was being offered at a $3.5 premium to two means but others said it was at an slightly lower fixed price, $83 cif.
